t:
Section 1207 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (22 U.S.C. 2151 note) is amended—
    (1) in subsection (i)—
        (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and 
        (B) by amending paragraph (2) to read as follows:“(2) Exception.—Amounts appropriated and transferred to the Fund before September 30, 2019, shall remain available for obligation and expenditure after that date, but only for activities under programs commenced under subsection (b) before September 30, 2019.”; and  
    (2) in subsection (o)—
        (A) in the first sentence, by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and 
        (B) in the second sentence, by striking “through 2019” and inserting “through 2021”.

fable.w: This section only extends expiration dates and clarifies the availability of previously appropriated funds for an existing program. There is no tempting participation reading: it contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to extend the expiration dates of a specific fund and related provisions. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text deals solely with internal federal appropriations and administrative deadlines.
qwen_block.s: Section 1207 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (22 U.S.C. 2151 note) is amended— (1) in subsection (i)— (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and (B) by amending paragraph (2) to read as follows:“(2) Exception.—Amounts appropriated and transferred to the Fund before September 30, 2019, shall remain available for obligation and expenditure after that date, but only for activities under programs commenced under subsection (b) before September 30, 2019.”; and (2) in subsection (o)— (A) in the first sentence, by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and (B) in the second sentence, by striking “through 2019” and inserting “through 2021”.

opus.w: The amendment only extends deadlines for the fund and says when appropriated money remains available. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. Any procedures in the underlying Section 1207 are not set out or changed by this text, so the date changes alone are not participation.
opus.s: in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”
opus.b:
I labelled this section **No**: it only changes dates and creates no process involving anyone outside the federal government.

The tempting reading is that the underlying Section 1207 (the Global Security Contingency Fund) may involve coordination or notice requirements, so amending it might seem to bring those in. That fails because the text here only pushes deadlines back, from 2019 to 2021, and sets a carryover rule for unspent money. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory deadlines for the availability of appropriated funds. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The changes are purely administrative and internal to the government's management of funds.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1207 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (22 U.S.C. 2151 note) is amended— (1) in subsection (i)— (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and (B) by amending paragraph (2) to read as follows:“(2) Exception.—Amounts appropriated and transferred to the Fund before September 30, 2019, shall remain available for obligation and expenditure after that date, but only for activities under programs commenced under subsection (b) before September 30, 2019.”; and (2) in subsection (o)— (A) in the first sentence, by striking “September 30, 2019” and inserting “September 30, 2021”; and (B) in the second sentence, by striking “through 2019” and inserting “through 2021”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing dates for a fund implies some procedural change involving outside parties, but the text is purely about the availability of appropriated funds and administrative deadlines. There is no mention of consultation, public comment, hearings, or interaction with non-federal entities. The actors involved are Congress (amending the statute) and the executive branch (managing the fund), all of which are inside the federal government.
